events.title: Hatha Yoga w/ Live Music
events.description:
$20-$25 at the door / $15 students & seniors / 12pm start  Experience the magic of a moving meditation with Integral Yoga instructor Vienna-Parashakti. This 90-minute class is appropriate for all students, from beginners to advanced yogis. Dress comfortably, and bring a cozy blanket if you’d like. (cash or venmo accepted at the door) 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Prepare to relax and rejuvenate your body, mind, and spirit in this peaceful yoga class. Explore the guided practice of Hatha Yoga and experience a series of classical Yoga asanas (physical postures), pranayama (breath control), Yoga Nidra (deep relaxation) and meditation.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Parashakti  (Vienna) is an Integral Yoga instructor and a new-ish resident to Cambridge from two and a half years studying and teaching at  Satchidananda Ashram  in Yogaville, Virginia.  She is currently teaching weekly Hatha Yoga classes at the Lilypad and other places around Cambridge. 
 
 
 
 
 
 Musical accompaniment on the Grand Piano provided by Jesse Gallagher, along with selections from his meditation album "The Inner Sound." 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 “ It was such a delight to attend your class.  My nervous system has been a wreck and it was wonderful to be in a place that felt safe for my body.  I haven’t moved my “yogi” body in years and it felt so good to wake up the cobwebs. Thank you for providing such a beautiful space for me in a day that I really needed it. ” 
 
 — Maria 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Yoga Classes at Lilypad continue weekly on Saturdays.

events.title: Toad: Saturday Revival - ‘The Bored of Health’
events.description: Toad Revival Series — Saturdays, 4–7 PM  Every Saturday from 4 to 7, we rewind the clock and let the old sparks fly. The  Toad Revival Series  is our tribute to the bands that built this stage, note by note, night after night. It’s a laid-back, early evening show filled with familiar sounds, longtime favorites, and the spirit of a scene that never really faded—just waited for the right time to plug back in. These are the artists who gave Toad its heartbeat, returning for intimate, no-frills sets that remind us why we’re here. Think front-porch energy with barroom volume, old songs with new life, and a crowd that knows when to sing along. Come early. Stay as long as you like. This is Toad, the way it was—and still is.

events.title: TCS presents: Josh Gondelman
events.description:
18+ w/ 2-Item Suggested Minimum.




Josh Gondelman
 is a writer and comedian who incubated in Boston before moving to New York City, where he currently lives and most recently worked as the head writer and an executive producer for 
Desus & Mero 
on Showtime. Previously, he spent five years at 
Last Week Tonight with John Oliver
, first as a web producer and then as a staff writer, where he earned four Emmy Awards, two Peabody Awards, and three WGA Awards. Josh also previously wrote for Fuse TV’s 
Billy On The Street
. His most recent hour, 
Positive Reinforcement
, is now available to stream. Josh’s debut stand-up special, 
People Pleaser, 
was released in 2022. In 2016, Josh made his late-night standup debut on 
Conan 
(TBS), and he has also performed on 
Late Night With Seth Meyers 
(NBC) and 
The Late Late Show with James Corden 
(CBS). Gondelman is the author of the essay collection 
Nice Try: Stories of Best Intentions and Mixed Results, 
published in September 2019 by Harper Perennial. Since 2019, he has been a regular panelist on NPR mainstay 
Wait Wait Don’t Tell Me
. Offstage, Gondelman is also the co-author (along with Joe Berkowitz) of the book 
You Blew It
, 
published in October 2015 by Plume. His writing has also appeared in prestigious publications such as McSweeney’s Internet Tendency, New York Magazine, and The New Yorker.

events.description:
$10 advance / $12 day of show / $8 student / 5pm doors/ 5:30 show / seated An intimate early evening set from JOURNEYGLO, featuring original songs performed with special guest Micah Yoo on acoustic guitar, plus a few collaborative moments. 
 
 
 
 
    Get Tickets
   
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 JOURNEYGLO  is a Dallas-based singer-songwriter creating intimate indie folk-pop with cinematic, ambient sensibilities. Her debut album,  Limp By Your Side , explores grief, faith, love, and the unresolved spaces between what was and what might be. For this stripped-down acoustic set, JOURNEYGLO brings the songs into a more vulnerable setting, centered on voice, guitar, haunting melodies, and honest storytelling that feels like sitting beside someone in the dark without rushing them toward resolution.   journeyglo.co @journeyglo  on instagram @journeyglo  on TikTok 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Micah Yoo 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 A classical violinist by training, a songwriter by hobby, and a licensed music therapist God willing — Micah Yoo is best described as an overall music enthusiast. Having taken an extended break from both writing and performing, Micah is excited to return to the stage alongside JOURNEYGLO and rediscover the joy of sharing music with a live audience.

events.title: UPSTAIRS SHOW: Ordinary Elephant
events.description:
Learn more / Buy Tickets
   
 
 
 
 
 "...their intimate songs, the weaving harmonies, and the stories that draw you in as if you were gathered around an enchanted campfire." - Eliza Gilkyson Mesmerizing folk duo Ordinary Elephant has spent the better part of the last decade on a never-ending tour that’s earned married couple Crystal and Pete Damore widespread critical acclaim and made fans of luminaries like Tom Paxton and Mary Gauthier. In 2017, the pair took home the International Folk Music Award for Artist of the Year on the strength of their breakout album, Before I Go, and two years later, they returned with the similarly lauded Honest, which the Associated Press hailed as “one of the best Americana albums of the year.” The band’s new stripped-down, self-titled collection is the purest distillation of their sound yet, showcasing the arresting power of the couple’s gorgeous harmonies and intricate fretwork. The songs are timeless, rooted in rich, character-driven storytelling, and the performances are similarly transportive, fueled by delicately intertwined banjo, guitar, and octave mandolin. Though the songs were born out of a period of deep uncertainty, the record itself is a work of profound self-assurance, one delivered by a duo whose personal and professional lives embody the limitless possibility of honest, organic collaboration. Press play on Ordinary Elephant and you’ll hear more than just a husband and wife; you’ll hear the sound of sincerity and commitment, of patience and gratitude, of learning to let go of expectation and revel in the simple beauty of the moment. https://www.ordinaryelephant.net/ $20 in advance. $25 at the  door. This Is An All Ages Show Doors are at 11:30am. Showtime is 12pm. Dinner and drinks available at all tables. NO REFUNDS OR EXCHANGES

A Boston area singer/guitarist, Chuck primarily performs solo but also plays out with his band, The Butler Frogs. He has opened for touring bands America, The Wallflowers, and The Gin Blossoms. In 2020, The Butler Frogs released their sole EP, Last Call For Opinions.

He was also a founding member of Northern Point (2005-2010), an acoustic trio from the NY/NJ area that released three albums (November, Northern Point: Live at St. James' Gate, and After The Frost). 

In 2016, Chuck founded and hosted (with musician Ronnie Hirschberg) the award-winning podcast Above The Basement - Boston Music and Conversation, which won a 202o Boston Music Award for Podcast/Radio Show of the Year.  After 200 episodes, Chuck shuttered the podcast and set out on his solo musical endeavor. 

 He currently performs in New England and is always on the lookout for the lost songs that have influenced him over the years.

events.title: Toad Sunday Revival - The Dennis Brennan Band
events.description: Dennis Brennan was born on the wrong side of the tracks in Marlboro, Massachusetts. At age 9 he entered show business as Rumplestiltsken in a grammar school play. In 7th grade he performed “Louie Louie” with a local garage band at the Berlin, Ma. Town Hall and quickly evolved into “the lead singer” That band evolved into “The Paranoids”, his musical outlet throughout his high school years. They opened shows for both The Remains and The Barbarians, garage band legends who are each featured on “Nuggets, original artyfacts from the first psychedelic era” Rhino R2 75486. Following high school. Brennan’s education continued as lead singer in such well regarded outfits as “The Dirty Rye Band”, The West Side Band”, “The Martells”, and “Push Push”. These bands performed in every bar and dive on the east coast. An education indeed. In 1992 he formed the Dennis Brennan Band and started his solo career, quickly releasing two critically acclaimed recordings on Upstart Records, a division of Rounder. In 2000 he released “Rule #1” on ESCA Records which resulted in glowing reviews from The New Yorker, The Chicago Sun Times, The Boston Phoenix as well as other publications nationwide. These recordings showcase Brennans ability “to not just tip toes into genres, he strips naked and plunges right in.” Bill Holmes, AMPLIFIER.

events.title: Joe Hunt Group
events.description:
$15 admission / Start 8:30pm / Doors 8pm / Seated Show Modern jazz played by Boston's best jazz musicians. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Joe Hunt  is a jazz drummer, educator, author, and historian. In the early 1960s, Joe Hunt performed and recorded alongside the late NEC Distinguished Artist-in-Residence Emeritus George Russell, with releases on Decca and Riverside. Hunt joined The Stan Getz Quartet in 1964, recording several releases on Verve, then was a member of the Bill Evans Trio from 1966-1967. The remainder of the 1960s found Hunt performing or recording with several other jazz luminaries including Chet Baker, Eric Dolphy, Dizzy Gillespie, Dexter Gordon, Charles Mingus, Bob Brookmeyer, and the late Herb Pomeroy. In the 1970s and 1980s, Hunt was a member of The National Jazz Ensemble, led jazz groups with John Scofield, Mike Stern, and Santi Debriano, and toured with quartets of Red Rodney and Hal McKusick. The 1990s, and beyond, have included membership in The Smithsonian Jazz Masters Orchestra, with former NEC president Gunther Schuller, performances with Kenny Burrell, Joe Lavano, Joanne Brackeen, and Tal Farlow, as well as recordings with the Bert Seager Quintet, and also, Trio. Hunt is the author of the 1994 book 52nd Street Beat, which is a historical look at jazz drummer greats from 1945 to 1965. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 The Joe Hunt quartet features a modern jazz ensemble music played by top local pros: Mark Pinto - alto saxophone, formerly years with the Buddy Rich band John Lockwood – bass, formerly with Joe Henderson, Lee Konitz, current Fringe member Yuka Hamano Hunt – piano, voice, arranger Joe Hunt – drums, formerly with George Russell, Stan Getz, Jim Hall, Dexter Gordon, and Bill Evans We pay tribute to a special composer or performer at most performances. Recent shows have included: Burt Bacharach, Ahmad Jamal, Bill Evans, and Gigi Gryce. Future shows will include the music of Paul and Carla Bley, and arranger, Johnny Mandel. - Continuing of the 3rd Sunday of Every Month

events.title: Elan Mehler Trio
events.description:
$15 / $10 students / 7pm  / seated 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Elan Mehler  has released 11 albums as a leader, with such musicians as Bill Frisell, Dave Douglas, Becca Stevens, Scott Robinson, Francisco Mela and many more and has garnered stellar reviews from such publications as The New York Times, The Guardian, Jazz Times, and Downbeat.  His latest record is a solo piano record released on Sunnyside Records that has garnered significant press.  Elan has brought his projects to clubs and festivals worldwide including Birdland, Queen Elizabeth Hall, and the North Sea Festival.  In 2016 Elan co-founded the label Newvelle Records, as artistic director of the label he has signed and produced over 50 records by artists such as Jack DeJohnette, John Patitucci, Dave Liebman, Lionel Loueke, Irma Thomas and Ellis Marsalis.  Reviews and music available at  www.elanmehler.com Max Ridley  is one of the most in-demand bassists in the Boston area. He was awarded full-tuition scholarships to study at Berklee College of Music for both undergraduate and graduate degrees, earning his graduate degree from the extremely exclusive Berklee Global Jazz Institute under the direction of master pianist, educator and humanitarian Danilo Perez. An equally important part of his education was down the street from Berklee at Boston’s historic Wally’s Jazz Cafe. He began going to jam sessions there in high school and eventually became the house bass player every Friday and Saturday night. Ridley has played and recorded with renowned musicians of many different styles all over the world.  An incredibly versatile multi-instrumentalist, Max performs regularly in bands playing Jazz, Rock, Folk, Soul, Punk, Klezmer, Polka and every other style you can think of.  He also serves as the music director for tap dance company Subject:Matter ( https://www.subjectmattertap.com/ ) and teaches music as a guest lecturer at different colleges around New England (such as Longy School of Music, University of New Hampshire and Berklee College of Music). Boston based Israeli drummer  Dor Herskovits  is already a staple of the Boston jazz scene and has won international acclaim as an improviser. His melodic approach to playing the drums, combined with vast knowledge of rhythm and a composer's vision make him a unique voice as a drummer. Dor's original music reflects the eclectic nature of music nowadays,  drawing from jazz and blues roots, folk and world music, free jazz rock and metal.   As a sought after sideman, he plays in various jazz and experimental groups on the Boston-New York line. He has also toured around the US, Canada, Europe and China. Herskovits has recorded many albums as a sideman, featured on labels such as Newvelle and Endectomorph music, alongside musicians such Grammy award-winning guitarist Bill Frisell, Michael Blake and Jason Palmer. He has also performed with George Garzone, Noah Preminger, Jon Cowherd, Steve Cardenas,Bert Seager’s Tet-rap-tych, Max Ridley’s Basement Philharmonic, Daniel Rotem and Xiongguan Zhang. As co-leader of Earprint, he received critical acclaim from publications such as Downbeat magazine, NPR’s critics' poll and many more.  www.dorherskovits.com 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Every Monday at 7PM Line-up subject to change

events.title: Jerry Bergonzi Quartet
events.description:
$15 @ the door / $10 students / 8:30 start / 8pm doors / seated  Jerry Bergonzi , Tenor Saxophone Luther Gray , Drums Special Guest , Trumpet Special Guest , Bass 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 A fine, high-powered tenor saxophonist with a tone influenced by John Coltrane, a mastery of chord changes, and a strong musical imagination,  Jerry Bergonzi  has long had an underground following in the Boston area. He started on clarinet when he was eight, switching to alto at 12, and finally to tenor two years later. Bergonzi was inspired early on by Sonny Rollins, Coltrane, and Hank Mobley. He attended Lowell University and then after graduation played electric bass in local bands behind singers and strippers, saving up enough money to move to New York in 1972. After struggling in the Big Apple for seven years and gaining some recognition as a member of Two Generations of Brubeck and of the Dave Brubeck Quartet (with whom he appeared on several Concord albums during 1979-1981), Bergonzi moved back to Boston in 1981, where he developed a strong career both as a tenorman and as an educator. He has since led several groups (including two called Con Brio and Gonz) and recorded for the Plug, Not Fat, Red, and Blue Note labels. —  By Scott Yanow, AllMusic 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Continuing Every Monday at 8:30pm Lineup subject to change

events.description:
$15 @ the door / $10 students / 10pm doors / 10:30 start / seated  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 The Fringe  originally formed back in 1971 by tenor-saxophonist  George Garzone , bassist Richard Appleman, and drummer Bob Gullotti as an outlet for their free jazz improvisations, The Fringe have entertained and enlightened Boston area jazz audiences for over 50 years. Bassist Appleman left the band in 1985 to become Chairman of the Bass Department at Berklee College and was replaced by veteran bassist  John Lockwood . Bob Gullotti passed away in 2020 and is remembered as one of the greatest jazz drummers of his generation. Francisco Mela, now on drums,  graciously fills the space Bob left behind. Along with their impressive tenure with The Fringe, Garzone, Lockwood, and Mela are in great demand as session players and have played with many of the greats of contemporary jazz. Along with keeping up with a busy performance schedule, each of them are well-respected educators helping to inspire the jazz musicians of tomorrow. events.description: Tickets available here Ready to meet local singles face-to-face? Join us for a fun, low-pressure evening of meaningful connections! Ditch the swiping. Come meet real, local singles in person. This is your excuse to get out, look good, grab a drink, and actually connect with people face to face. No more endless texting and never meeting in-person, no more guessing.. just a fun, social night where you can talk, laugh, flirt, and see what happens. Our speed dating events are designed to feel natural and effortless. It’s everything you wish dating apps felt like… but in real life. Note on Age Range:  While this event is geared toward the age range listed in the title, it’s not a strict rule. If you feel like you’d vibe with this crowd, you’re welcome to join. Our goal is always to create a well-balanced group where connections actually make sense. 🎟️ Ticket Pricing Reserve your spot early! Ticket prices increase once the first 20 tickets have been sold. Our events are intentionally kept at a comfortable size to ensure everyone has enough time to meet each participant. As events fill up, ticket prices increase, so we recommend reserving your spot early to lock in the best price. Don’t wait. Secure your ticket before the first 20 spots are gone! ⸻ How the Night Works Start with a Social Mixer Kick things off with a relaxed mingle. Grab a drink (not included, but highly encouraged), settle in, and get comfortable before the rounds begin. Easy, Guided Conversations We keep things flowing so you don’t have to overthink it. Each round includes a fun icebreaker, and our host guides the room so everything feels smooth, upbeat, and never awkward. Quick, Real Connections You’ll spend a few minutes with each person, just enough time to catch a vibe before rotating. It’s light, fun, and way more natural than sitting through a full date. Match the Ones You’re Into After each round, you’ll mark “friend,” “date,” or “none” on our simple matching system. If it’s mutual, we’ll send you each other’s info the next day.

events.description:
$15 admission / 10pm doors / 10:30 start / standing / all ages “Dark red from paint” is the exploration of unorthodox sounds in order to comprehend unintelligible feelings. This mix of alt rock groups bring ethereal soundscapes and transgressive distortion to take the audience into unnamed yet understood  memories. This wide range of bands provide a space where everyone has a place. Through energetic and heartfelt music be ready for an ecstatic rock set into the night. TRACING  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Tracing is a post-rock project by Almeda Tracing. @almedatracing   LA MANIK 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 La Manik is a 5 piece art rock band that creates catchy hooks and transgressive noise to connect with viewers through raw emotional expression. Originally formed with the goal to soundtrack Latin American short stories that narrate this society’s outliers, the band has now grown into a creative vehicle for the members to express themselves through songs that touch on: lost love, identity, and dark desires difficult to express in the day to day. From Sonic Youth sprawls to 6/8 Isley Brothers choruses, Beatles inspired basslines and Descartes a Kant theatrics. La Manik puts into dialogue diverse influences in the songs themselves, showing the beauty of being different and the malleable nature of musical heritage. Instagram:   @la.manikk Soundcloud:   https://on.soundcloud.com/NGRr1BoxlHf8MXR5vE Youtube:   https://youtu.be/PX5x52HZKPs?si=gRsbmXz3ffg4Oeh6   SIKAYDA

events.description:
$20-$25 at the door / $15 students & seniors / All Levels Experience the magic of a moving meditation with Integral Yoga instructor and musician Sadhu (Jesse) Gallagher. This 90-minute class is appropriate for all students, from beginners to advanced yogis. Dress comfortably, and bring a cozy blanket if you’d like. 
 
 
 
 
    Reserve a spot
   
 
 
 
 
 
 (cash or venmo accepted at the door) 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Prepare to relax and rejuvenate your body, mind, and spirit in this peaceful yoga class. Explore the guided practice of Hatha Yoga and experience a series of classical Yoga asanas (physical postures), pranayama (breath control), Yoga Nidra (deep relaxation) and meditation.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Sadhu-Jesse Gallagher  is an Integral Yoga teacher and life-long musician. He traveled & performed extensively as a founding member of the band Apollo Sunshine from 2001-2010, and since has released several albums under his own name (The Inner Sound 2020, Visual Music Vol. #1 & #2). He has practiced meditation & yoga since 2000. In 2016, he was certified to teach Integral Yoga Hatha at Satchidananda Ashram, and in 2024, Jesse was certified to teach Mindfulness Meditation from Dharma Moon Tibet House. 
 
 
 
 
 
 Musical accompaniment on the Grand Piano also provided by Jesse Gallagher, along with selections from his meditation album "The Inner Sound." 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 “ It was such a delight to attend your class.  My nervous system has been a wreck and it was wonderful to be in a place that felt safe for my body.  I haven’t moved my “yogi” body in years and it felt so good to wake up the cobwebs. Thank you for providing such a beautiful space for me in a day that I really needed it. ”

Eddie Pepitone
 is a master of the dark art of comedy. Hailed as a modern day cross between Jackie Gleason, Don Rickles and Eckhart Tolle. Eddie is a force of nature on stage, switching between social rage and self-doubt. His shows are an energetic combo of calm and chaos, blue-collar angst and sardonic enlightenment. Few comedians working today channel the power of the rant better than Eddie Pepitone.




Eddie's latest stand-up special, 
The Collapse
,
 is out now on streaming platform VEEPS and YouTube. The special is a true Pepitone rant and romp as he barrels through the heightened emotions and anxieties of modern life in a somehow joyful and jovial energy that only Pepitone can deliver. In addition to his regular stand-up shows, Pepitone is a stand-out comedic character actor. Beginning in New York City’s improv and sketch scene where he quickly became a regular face, and continuing on to recurring roles on Late Night with Conan O’Brien and appearances on WTF with Marc Maron Podcast. Most recently, Eddie can be seen in Max's Haley Quinn spin-off Kite Man, Hell Yea!, Hulu's Ramy, and Nickelodeon’s Rock Paper Scissors. Eddie has also appeared on numerous comedy TV shows, including Crazy Ex-Girlfriend, Rick and Morty, Reno 911!, 10 Year Old Tom, The Life and Times of Tim, Will & Grace, It’s Always Sunny in Philadelphia, Love, The Sarah Silverman Program, Jimmy Kimmel Live, After Midnight, Last Comic Standing, Chappelle’s Show, appearances on Bob’s Burgers, and he’s a regular on Adult Swim’s Your Pretty Face is Going to Hell. Fans also might recognize Pepitone from his role in the hit comedy Old School, where he plays the role of 'Archer', one of the recruiting pledges.

 Elan Mehler  has released 11 albums as a leader, with such musicians as Bill Frisell, Dave Douglas, Becca Stevens, Scott Robinson, Francisco Mela and many more and has garnered stellar reviews from such publications as The New York Times, The Guardian, Jazz Times, and Downbeat.  His latest record is a solo piano record released on Sunnyside Records that has garnered significant press.  Elan has brought his projects to clubs and festivals worldwide including Birdland, Queen Elizabeth Hall, and the North Sea Festival.  In 2016 Elan co-founded the label Newvelle Records, as artistic director of the label he has signed and produced over 50 records by artists such as Jack DeJohnette, John Patitucci, Dave Liebman, Lionel Loueke, Irma Thomas and Ellis Marsalis.  Reviews and music available at  www.elanmehler.com Max Ridley  is one of the most in-demand bassists in the Boston area. He was awarded full-tuition scholarships to study at Berklee College of Music for both undergraduate and graduate degrees, earning his graduate degree from the extremely exclusive Berklee Global Jazz Institute under the direction of master pianist, educator and humanitarian Danilo Perez. An equally important part of his education was down the street from Berklee at Boston’s historic Wally’s Jazz Cafe. He began going to jam sessions there in high school and eventually became the house bass player every Friday and Saturday night. Ridley has played and recorded with renowned musicians of many different styles all over the world.  An incredibly versatile multi-instrumentalist, Max performs regularly in bands playing Jazz, Rock, Folk, Soul, Punk, Klezmer, Polka and every other style you can think of.  He also serves as the music director for tap dance company Subject:Matter ( https://www.subjectmattertap.com/ ) and teaches music as a guest lecturer at different colleges around New England (such as Longy School of Music, University of New Hampshire and Berklee College of Music). Boston based Israeli drummer  Dor Herskovits  is already a staple of the Boston jazz scene and has won international acclaim as an improviser. His melodic approach to playing the drums, combined with vast knowledge of rhythm and a composer's vision make him a unique voice as a drummer. Dor's original music reflects the eclectic nature of music nowadays,  drawing from jazz and blues roots, folk and world music, free jazz rock and metal.   As a sought after sideman, he plays in various jazz and experimental groups on the Boston-New York line. He has also toured around the US, Canada, Europe and China. Herskovits has recorded many albums as a sideman, featured on labels such as Newvelle and Endectomorph music, alongside musicians such Grammy award-winning guitarist Bill Frisell, Michael Blake and Jason Palmer. He has also performed with George Garzone, Noah Preminger, Jon Cowherd, Steve Cardenas,Bert Seager’s Tet-rap-tych, Max Ridley’s Basement Philharmonic, Daniel Rotem and Xiongguan Zhang. As co-leader of Earprint, he received critical acclaim from publications such as Downbeat magazine, NPR’s critics' poll and many more.  www.dorherskovits.com

 A fine, high-powered tenor saxophonist with a tone influenced by John Coltrane, a mastery of chord changes, and a strong musical imagination,  Jerry Bergonzi  has long had an underground following in the Boston area. He started on clarinet when he was eight, switching to alto at 12, and finally to tenor two years later. Bergonzi was inspired early on by Sonny Rollins, Coltrane, and Hank Mobley. He attended Lowell University and then after graduation played electric bass in local bands behind singers and strippers, saving up enough money to move to New York in 1972. After struggling in the Big Apple for seven years and gaining some recognition as a member of Two Generations of Brubeck and of the Dave Brubeck Quartet (with whom he appeared on several Concord albums during 1979-1981), Bergonzi moved back to Boston in 1981, where he developed a strong career both as a tenorman and as an educator. He has since led several groups (including two called Con Brio and Gonz) and recorded for the Plug, Not Fat, Red, and Blue Note labels. —  By Scott Yanow, AllMusic

Michelle Shocked's Bootleg This!
events.description:
$30 advance / $35 at the door / 6pm doors / 6:30 start / seated 
 
 
 
 
    Get tickets
   
 
 
 
 
 
 Surviving a 13 year blacklist, activist & musician  Michelle Shocked  has emerged with the release of her audio memoir Bootleg This! Forty years after her legendary bootleg debut, the Grammy winner returns with a vengeance.  An act of defiance -- this tour is breaking the blacklist, disturbing the silence. Slinging stories and songs set carefully like stones; a fusillade of human emotion in an air-punching Fuck Yeah. Calm, confident, controlled with a lethal focus. Balanced and battle-bitten, sharing tales of media misadventures fused by a set of select songs. "You can't take the art out of the artist. Creative labor has value; stolen art has potent power." "I knew it would work — I just didn't know it would work so well." 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Born in Dallas and raised in the soaking humid Piney Woods of east Texas,  Michelle Shocked  grew up in a large fundamentalist Mormon family before leaving home at sixteen. She put herself through the University of Texas at Austin, earning a degree in Oral Interpretation of Literature while becoming increasingly involved in political activism.                     Before she was a celebrated recording artist, Shocked was a fixture of the American punk underground. Flying a mohawk and a safety pin for a nose ring, while busking on the streets with her mandolin and fiddle, she sprang, fully-formed, from the San Francisco hardcore scene. She was arrested in 1984 at the Democratic National Convention in San Francisco and  again  at the Republican National Convention in Dallas, and the iconic  San Francisco Examiner  photo of her arrest, in a police chokehold, subsequently became the cover image of her debut studio album,  Short Sharp Shocked .                     “You can be poor anywhere,” she figured, making her way to Paris to join the resistance against Reagan’s Cold War provocations: squatting in Amsterdam while working with a pirate radio collective, joining fellow pirate radio activists in Madrid to celebrate the 10th Anniversary of Franco’s death, enlisting at a women’s peace camp in Sicily, vagabonding Europe—from Finland to Morocco—on a counterfeit rail pass poached in Brixton, and survived on the remnants of the Old Left’s mutual aid network. Music was never the plan. Activism was.                     That unlikely journey would eventually produce one of the most unconventional careers in contemporary American music—one that has continually crossed the boundaries between folk, blues, swing, gospel, politics, faith, and storytelling while remaining defiantly independent at every turn. Activist and musician Michelle Shocked emerges with the release of her audio memoir,  Bootleg This!  https://michelleshocked.supercast.com /  "Michelle Shocked is a true trailblazer who knows how to play with fire"  ~ Rolling Stone more press:   Roadworks fall tour promo video   artist profile feature   recent:  profile in the Scotsman

events.title: Lilypad Jazz Jam
events.description:
$5 - 15 sliding scale admission / 3-7pm / all ages 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 We're excited to be welcoming the Lilypad community to jam and listen to music together.  The  Lilypad Jazz Jam  is open to instrumentalists of all levels, we only ask that you come prepared to play at least one or two well-known Jazz Standards in the commonly played key. Listeners are welcome to come and enjoy the music these spontaneously arranged ensembles will create! Our host will be working with players to make sure everyone gets a chance to get on stage and play something they're comfortable with. We'll have a drum kit, piano and bass on the back line. Our stage hosts some of the heaviest players on the planet, come down and catch the vibe! We're happy to have Nic Adams hosting and leading a band to get the night started. Come early, you won't want to miss their performance! Nic Adams  is a multi-instrumentalist, performer, composer, educator, and luthier based in Boston, MA. Specializing in saxophone, drums, guitar, bass, and north Asian folk music, their music pulls from a long list of traditions, from John Coltrane to punk rock and Tuvan throat singing. With this wide array of influences, Nic seeks to create music that synthesizes many different musical points into a cohesive and unique form. Finding common grounds among musical cultures and using them as jumping-off points for new compositions or improvisations is at the core of Nic’s work. Nic is currently pursuing a Master’s at Longy School of Music, gigs in the greater Boston area, and spends their free time building hybrid Tuvan/western traditional instruments. Please direct any questions to  persistentfool@protonmail.com

events.title: Under The Influence
events.description:
$10 cover / 3:30pm doors / 4pm start / seated 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Poetry Readings with accompanying music Words: Geoff Chasin Music: Stella Owen and John Turner w Special Guests Geoff Chasin  is a local poet who believes that poetry is the perfect tool for exploring our inner and outer worlds. He is excited to work with Stella, John and others to explore different types of heros, and the different landscapes of the heroic journey. Stella Owen  is a classically trained pianist with a Master’s in Music from Northwestern University. Her love of all genres of music, and of ensemble playing, has compelled her to branch off in many directions: she plays keyboard with a number of orchestras including the Cape Cod Symphony, plays four hand piano in many venues, sings with the New World Chorale, plays jazz clarinet with Tuesday Night Special, and has been known to get down occasionally with some local rock and roll bands. Working with “Under the Influence” is yet one more experiment in her ever-blossoming musical career. A veteran of the New England jazz scene, bassist  John Turner  has performed and recorded with just about everybody--specifically the Either/Orchestra, Charlie Kohlhase, Scott Hamilton, Roswell Rudd, Lee Konitz, the Tommy Dorsey Orchestra, members of Ornette Coleman’s band, the White Heat Swing Orchestra, and for over sixteen years was a member of Roomful of Blues, a five time Grammy nominated band.

events.title: Toad Sunday Revival - Tim Gearan Band
events.description: A beloved fixture in the Boston music scene for over 25 years, Tim Gearan has become a bonafide local music hero. His warm, raspy baritone, jaw-dropping guitar skills and wry, poignant songwriting have graced the bars, pubs, and music halls throughout New England and beyond, creating a loyal cult-like following. Gearan, a New York native, spent ten years touring the globe as a sideman for the great Toni Lynn Washington, as well as collaborating with Grammy-winning singer/guitarist Susan Tedeschi. Finding his own artistic voice, Gearan  has crafted an intoxicating blend of Americana, folk and blues with shades of Randy Newman, Tom Waits, JJ Cale,  Leon Russell and Lowell George. He quickly established himself as a force in the Boston’s resurgent roots music scene, and his Boston area residencies have become a “can’t miss” staple of the city’s nightlife. Gearan has released 7 albums to date, as well as 4 single releases; “While the World Goes By” (2019)  “It’s Not the End of the World"  (2019) “Hey, Hey, Hey” (2020) and “Talk About Heaven” (2020).

's Live From South High: 
After 12 years as a public school teacher, comedian Orlando Baxter left the classroom and eventually built a career he never imagined for himself: stand-up comedy.
 Live From South High blends stand-up and storytelling to tell the unlikely journey that took Orlando from student, to teacher, to the comedy stage—and what it means to leave one version of your life behind and start another.
 Orlando made his national television debut on Conan, has appeared on BET, performed at comedy festivals around the world and at TD Garden as part of Comics Come Home, and his Dry Bar Comedy special has been viewed more than five million times.
 Funny, personal, and relatable, Live From South High is a show about teaching, work, identity, taking risks, and starting over.

The Globe described the night as “Comedy Hell” when we were upstairs in Somerville’s Union Square.  Bayge

Through various influences that he has continually absorbed through his music studies, he has come to be the musician that he is today. Born and raised in Los Angeles, California Joaquin realized his love for music early on. Starting on ukulele and eventually turning to guitar, he was raised in various youth music programs, throughout the city such as NTyme, The Colburn School, The Fernando Pullum Community Arts Center, and the Los Angeles County High School for The Arts. Through these various programs, he has had the opportunity to play at many esteemed venues such as the Hollywood Bowl, Catalina Jazz Club, and Thew Mint, as well as playing and performing with many esteemed artists such as Paul Cornish, Keith David, Gretchen Parlato and more. He has won many awards as a composer and a performer (Downbeat Magazine, YoungArts, Music Center Spotlight) and is currently continuing his studies at the Berklee College of Music with a full tuition scholarship. He seeks to continue improving on his art and to expand his worldviews, by befriending and collaborating with his peers, as well as absorbing the knowledge of his professors. events.title: Anna May
events.description:
Alternative tragic Americana, invocations for peace & judgment reshaping with bleeding heart stream of consciousness poems. The deep exploration of heartbreak and trauma has been an ongoing quest throughout Anna's work. Her lyrics have been heavily textured by a lonesome whimsicality that finds itself most at home in the vastness of the American West or in landscapes of stark frontiers. Anna's music honors the nomadic spirit with memory, meditation & fresh interpretations of folk music & jazz influence. She honors a hope to enhance connection, humility, healing, and joy among people in the process of parting with typical genre rules. Anna's lyrical sensibility is steeped in wisdom, and layered with evocative musicality and metaphysical embroidery while eschewing the mainstream & parting with platitudes. Anna explores both estrangement and connection while taking cues from artists like Billie Holiday, Shawn Colvin, & Neil Young. Anna has been compared to artists like Jeff Buckley & Aimee Mann. Anna has opened for artists like Kacy Hill, Amythyst Kiah, The Arcadian Wild, People Museum, & Jann Klose.

Anna has performed at wildflower music & arts festival, treefort music festival, Brick and Mortar Music Hall in San Francisco, High Dive in Seattle, the Mint in Los Angeles, Spiderhouse Ballroom in Austin, Rockwood Music Hall in New York City, Larimer Lounge in Denver, PNC Live Studio, & many more. 
Anna has been featured in publications like V13 media, WFMU, Medium, Northern Public Radio, & many more. Anna May was nominated for best Indie song of 2023 by Indie Boulevard Magazine. In 2024, Anna was a featured guest on NPR's Great American Folk Show, on WKU PBS Lost River Sessions (episode to air in 2025) & her song, The Show was chosen as song of the day on KUTX in Austin in 2024. In 2024, Anna was nominated for Best Americana Act at the New England Music Awards & was featured on the WDVX Blue Plate Special.

events.title: UPSTAIRS: Somerville Songwriter Sessions
events.description:
Learn more / Buy Tickets
   
 
 
 
 
 As it has for more than a decade, Somerville Songwriter Sessions presents the finest acoustic singer-songwriters each month in an intimate, welcoming setting. Each concert features three songwriters each doing a solo set, and then trading songs in the round, allowing for stories, impromptu harmonies, jamming, and spontaneous inspiration. Each show, one of our five hosts – Rachel Marie, Terry Kitchen, Sam Bayer, Beth DeSombre, Jack Byrne – are joined by some of the best local and touring singer-songwriters on the scene. October 11: Terry Kitchen Called "one of New England's best songwriters" by The Boston Globe, Terry Kitchen has been performing on folk stages across the country since the 1990s, releasing a dozen albums filled with literate musical storytelling, supple guitar playing and distinctive, intimate vocals. His 2025 album We All Dream (with its title song reaching the top ten of the national Folk-DJ chart) offers a hard-won glimmer of hope just when we need it most. His songs have won the Mid-Atlantic and USA Song Contests and been runner-up in the John Lennon Song Contest, and have appeared in numerous films. In the 1980s he was the leader of the groundbreaking Boston band Loose Ties, whose experiences he recounts in his novel Next Big Thing, called "a great debut novel" by The San Francisco Book Review. "Terry Kitchen begins where Tom Waits and Elvis Costello merge and leave off."-Vance Gilbert November 8: Rachel Marie Rachel Marie (she/they) follows in a tradition of unapologetically forthright femme folksingers, with songs that hearken to "overstuffed lines of Tori Amos, philosophical turn of Indigo Girls, and lilting vocals like Joni Mitchell" (Victoria Farmer, The Christian Humanist Podcast). The social awareness of folk meets the introspection and healing of the singer-songwriter tradition, featuring the emotional catharsis and dynamic vocals of a Broadway show. With a songwriting approach as raw and honest as it's always been, Rachel Marie is making a return to live performance after an unintentional hibernation hiatus, ready to reconnect with a real live audience. December 13: Beth DeSombre Beth DeSombre writes songs that are "smart and  uplifting...focusing on the quiet meaning to be found in ordinary life" (Sing Out! Magazine), exploring issues from the personal to the political. Her music touches both mind and heart, with insights wrapped in melody and harmony that stay with you after the echoes of the last chorus have faded away. Her newest CD Holding the Threads (2024) is her most personal album to date, telling stories about family and crisis and trying to find hope in dark times. Her previous EP The Sea Beside Us (2023), tells stories of ships and the ocean. Her 2017 EP Resistance, which was written in response to the political situation after the 2016 election, is a fundraiser for the ACLU. An award-winning writer in many formats, she has published 8 books. $15 in advance. (+ processing fees) $20 at the door. This Is An All Ages Show Doors are at 3:30pm. Showtime is 4pm. Dinner and drinks available at all tables. NO REFUNDS OR EXCHANGES

events.title: Girls Night Out: Tate Smith, Haley Montelaro, & Maggie Marre
events.description:
$10 advance / $12 at the door / 9:30 doors / 10pm show / seated & standing Three Berklee singer/songwriters with heartfelt stories of love and life share the stage, each performing a 25 minute set. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Tate Smith 
 is a rising force in country music. A gifted songwriter, vocalist, and performer with undeniable star quality recognized by her growing fanbase. Her captivating, angelic, and emotionally charged voice paired with her “what you see is what you get” stage presence, delivers equal parts laughter, introspection, and fresh perspective with every performance. Grounded in her sharp-witted observations and honest storytelling, Tate has a way of turning life’s messiest moments into songs that feel personal and universally relatable. Tate was raised in a small town, and later relocated to Boston where she is currently in her second-year pursuing a Bachelors of Music in Songwriting at Berklee College of Music. Being raised in a musically diverse family, Tate is carving out a space all her own in the evolving landscape of country music, seamlessly blending country’s kickback attitude, folk storytelling, and alternative rebellion. Most recently, Tate shared the bill with country music sensations Dallas Smith, Tim Hicks, and the Glorious Sons, at the North of Nowhere Country Music Festival, where she placed second in the festival’s Emerging Artist Showcase. Tate is currently working towards the release of her debut EP, collaborating with fellow artists, and performing live at local restaurants and coffee houses. With a distinctive voice and plenty of stories left to tell, she’s proving to be an artist worth watching. Find Tate on instagram  @tatesmithsings   
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Haley Montelaro   
 is a 20-year-old pop artist from Bellevue, WA. As soon as she was old enough to reach the keys of the piano, she never stopped playing and singing. Her mind was always filled with melodies and lyrics, and she wrote her first full song in 7th grade. She started attending Berklee College of Music in 2024 to pursue a career in artistry and songwriting. After meeting some friends in her dorm that inspired her to record and release her music, she never looked back. Inspired by artists like Claire Rosinkranz, Olivia Rodrigo, Lizzy Mcalpine, and Lindsey Lomis, Haley has released 11 songs since December of 2024. She feels like she's finally found her sound with her 2 most recent singles, "Any Way Out" and "MOUTH"--featuring her jazz upbringing by blending elements like scatting and chromatics into her pop songs.  linktr.ee/haleymontelaro 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Maggie Marre 
 is an indie-pop singer-songwriter from Reading, Pennsylvania, and a student at Berklee College of Music. Inspired by artists like Taylor Swift, Gracie Abrams, Holly Humberstone, and Sabrina Carpenter, she turns life’s awkward, exciting, messy, and meaningful moments into catchy, emotionally honest songs. Her debut single, Boy on the Moon (2024), introduced listeners to her dreamy storytelling style, followed by her debut EP, Miss Paranoia (2025), a collection of songs exploring overthinking, growing up, self-discovery, and everything in between. In 2025, Maggie was nominated for two Central Pennsylvania Music Awards—EP of the Year for Miss Paranoia and Best Pop Artist—and was a finalist in the Women Who Rock Songwriting Competition. Splitting her time between Pennsylvania and Boston, she performs throughout the Northeast, connecting with audiences through relatable lyrics, infectious melodies, and a personality that’s equal parts heartfelt and fun. When’s she’s not performing, she’s writing and recording new music, with more original releases on the way.

events.description: [vc_row][vc_column][ultimate_heading source="post_title" heading_tag="h1" main_heading_color="#BE1E2D" main_heading_font_family="font_family:|font_call:" main_heading_style="font-weight:bold;"][/ultimate_heading][ultimate_spacer height="10" height_on_tabs="10" height_on_tabs_portrait="10" height_on_mob_landscape="7" height_on_mob="7"][dt_fancy_separator separator_color="accent" line_thickness="3"][ultimate_spacer height="10" height_on_tabs="10" height_on_tabs_portrait="10" height_on_mob_landscape="7" height_on_mob="7"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row][vc_column][dt_fancy_image image_id="29750" onclick="lightbox" width="" caption="on"][ultimate_spacer height="32" height_on_tabs="32" height_on_tabs_portrait="32" height_on_mob_landscape="28" height_on_mob="28"][vc_column_text]        Examine the classic American play A Raisin in the Sun and its unofficial sequel through the lenses of urban migration and change.              Join the West End Museum and the Museum of African American History for a discussion series on two plays that examines the cycle of Black migration, white flight, urban renewal, displacement, and gentrification in Chicago’s changing neighborhoods.    First, read Lorraine Hansberry’s classic play A Raisin in the Sun, a Black family drama set on the South Side of Chicago. The Younger family lives in poverty, but when a life insurance payment offers them a chance to change their situation, they face the question of how to achieve their deferred dreams. Do they invest in business, education, or a home in a white neighborhood? Discuss how redlining, poverty, and neglect of urban neighborhoods has affected Black communities.    Next read Bruce Norris’s Claybourne Park, a new perspective on Hansberry’s story that follows a white family selling their home in a quiet neighborhood in Chicago. It soon becomes clear that they are selling to the Younger family prompting discussions on block busting, white flight, the American Dream, and what happens when the cycles of urban change come to affect the same house and communities.    This two part book club is open to all.    Reserve a free ticket to join with your own copies of the plays or select paid tickets and pick up copies of each book at the West End Museum. But what about Belinda Sutton or Edmonia Lewis? Join us for the opening of this special exhibition, in which we invite visitors to discover the lives and legacies of individuals who may not appear in our textbooks but whose contributions helped shape the American story.    As we reflect on a nation’s fight for independence 250 years ago, we also look forward—through the eyes of these emerging artists—toward a future shaped by awareness, creativity, and the power of untold stories.    Each teen artist from Artists for Humanity has chosen someone who resonates with them personally, crafting thoughtful statements that highlight their connection to their subject. At this opening, hear directly from teen artists and learn more about their process and inspiration.    View powerful paintings, digital prints, and drawings by young creators at the West End Museum, curated by Artists for Humanity.    Light refreshments will be available. events.description: Register here Nebula's spooky season book club! Join us as we read & discuss  Slewfoot: A Tale of Bewitchery  over craft beers at the Idle Hands taproom (non-alcoholic options available). A paid ticket includes a BRAND NEW copy of the book, or you can register for free and bring your own (if you prefer a non-physical format, you can support us by purchasing through our affiliate links on  Bookshop.org  or  libro.fm )! Meetings will be held on 9/30, 10/14, and 10/28. Copies of the book will be distributed at the first meeting; if you're not able to make that session, contact us to set up an alternate pickup time. Register here Book description: A  USA TODAY  BESTSELLER! Set in Colonial New England,  Slewfoot  is a tale of magic and mystery, of triumph and terror as only dark fantasist Brom can tell it. Connecticut, 1666: An ancient spirit awakens in a dark wood. The wildfolk call him Father, slayer, protector. The colonists call him Slewfoot, demon, devil. To Abitha, a recently widowed outcast, alone and vulnerable in her pious village, he is the only one she can turn to for help. Together, they ignite a battle between pagan and Puritan – one that threatens to destroy the entire village, leaving nothing but ashes and bloodshed in their wake. This terrifying tale of bewitchery features more than two dozen of Brom’s haunting full-color paintings and brilliant endpapers, fully immersing readers in this wild and unforgiving world.

She is currently teaching weekly Hatha Yoga classes at the Lilypad and other places around Cambridge. 
 
 
 
 
 
 Musical accompaniment on the Grand Piano provided by Jesse Gallagher, along with selections from his meditation album "The Inner Sound."

I haven’t moved my “yogi” body in years and it felt so good to wake up the cobwebs. Thank you for providing such a beautiful space for me in a day that I really needed it. ”

Comedian and former BuzzFeed Chief Creative Officer Jeff Greenspan shares behind-the-scenes stories from viral pranks he’s pulled on corporate crooks, privacy invaders, and other modern messes. He took what he learned working in media and used it to mess with the media, hijacking news cycles with stunts so bold even NYC’s mayor had to weigh in. events.description:
$15 admission / Start 8:30pm / Doors 8pm / Seated Show Modern jazz played by Boston's best jazz musicians. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Joe Hunt  is a jazz drummer, educator, author, and historian. In the early 1960s, Joe Hunt performed and recorded alongside the late NEC Distinguished Artist-in-Residence Emeritus George Russell, with releases on Decca and Riverside. Hunt joined The Stan Getz Quartet in 1964, recording several releases on Verve, then was a member of the Bill Evans Trio from 1966-1967. The remainder of the 1960s found Hunt performing or recording with several other jazz luminaries including Chet Baker, Eric Dolphy, Dizzy Gillespie, Dexter Gordon, Charles Mingus, Bob Brookmeyer, and the late Herb Pomeroy. In the 1970s and 1980s, Hunt was a member of The National Jazz Ensemble, led jazz groups with John Scofield, Mike Stern, and Santi Debriano, and toured with quartets of Red Rodney and Hal McKusick. The 1990s, and beyond, have included membership in The Smithsonian Jazz Masters Orchestra, with former NEC president Gunther Schuller, performances with Kenny Burrell, Joe Lavano, Joanne Brackeen, and Tal Farlow, as well as recordings with the Bert Seager Quintet, and also, Trio. Hunt is the author of the 1994 book 52nd Street Beat, which is a historical look at jazz drummer greats from 1945 to 1965. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 The Joe Hunt quartet features a modern jazz ensemble music played by top local pros: Mark Pinto - alto saxophone, formerly years with the Buddy Rich band John Lockwood – bass, formerly with Joe Henderson, Lee Konitz, current Fringe member Yuka Hamano Hunt – piano, voice, arranger Joe Hunt – drums, formerly with George Russell, Stan Getz, Jim Hall, Dexter Gordon, and Bill Evans We pay tribute to a special composer or performer at most performances. Recent shows have included: Burt Bacharach, Ahmad Jamal, Bill Evans, and Gigi Gryce. Future shows will include the music of Paul and Carla Bley, and arranger, Johnny Mandel. - Continuing of the 3rd Sunday of Every Month

events.title: Nondualism Trio presents Nosferatu Funk
events.description:
$15 admission / 7pm doors / 7:30 start / seated & standing The Boston-based progressive jazz group  Nondualism Trio   presents "Nosferatu Funk"  at the Lilypad! Featuring Mark Tipton (trumpet), James Heazlewood-Dale (bass), and Paul July Joseph (drums), Nondualism Trio will be playing original works, including Mark's compositions from their upcoming album, "Nosferatu Funk." The set will include: "Paraconsistent Refractions," "Walk-A-Seven Ghost Dance," "Lithospheric Waltz," "Cosmic Dust Groove Thang," "Into the Wilderness," "Slow Burn," "Nosferatu Funk," a pair of musical "Mantras," and more! Expect deep grooves, musical complexity, and synergistic ensemble playing.    
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Nondualism Trio  is a Boston-based progressive jazz trio that includes Mark Tipton on trumpet, James Heazlewood-Dale on bass, and Paul July Joseph on drums. Mark is originally from Maine, James is originally from Australia, and Paul is from Haiti. Nondualism Trio was formed in 2025 and in February 2026 they recorded their first album at Q Division Studios in Cambridge, MA, featuring Mark’s original compositions. They have recently performed at The Lilypad in Cambridge, The Drake in Amherst, and NEC’s Pierce Hall. The ensemble’s name, Nondualism Trio, is derived from the Indian philosophy that views reality as an interconnected whole, devoid of dualistic thinking, whereby awareness can be experienced beyond conceptual thought. It is this state of mind that Nondualism Trio seeks to embody when they are performing together: collectively open-minded in their improvisations to carry the music wherever it wants to go, and free from judgements and intuited mental road-blocks. Their music is both structured and open. The three members of Nondualism Trio are all rising talents in jazz, and are all active musicians on the Boston scene, seasoned touring musicians, and devoted teachers (Mark at NEC, James at Brandeis, and Paul through his private studio). James and Mark have recently toured Turkey, Cypress, and the Northeastern US with Mehmet Ali Sanlıkol and both his jazz quintet and classical Turkish music ensemble, DÜNYA, while Paul and Mark have recently toured New England. They enjoy connecting with diverse audiences and inspiring young musicians. Mark Tipton  is a Boston-based jazz trumpeter, composer, and educator who has recently been appointed as Assistant Chair of Jazz Studies at NEC. He has recently performed and/or recorded with Jerry Bergonzi, Dave Holland, Antonio Sanchez, Eguie Castrillo, Jason Moran, Allan Chase, Edmar Colón, Diego Figueiredo, Joe Hunt, Ayn Inserto, Tom Varner, and Mehmet Sanlikol. His Boston-based jazz octet released its debut album Vernacular Stretch in December 2025 at Soapbox Gallery in Brooklyn, and his progressive jazz group Nondualism Trio recorded their debut album in February 2026, featuring Mark on trumpet, James Heazlewood-Dale on bass, and Paul July Joseph on drums. Mark has toured the US, Europe, Turkey, and Cypress with numerous ensembles, and he holds a DMA degree from NEC. He enjoys sharing the joys of creative improvisation with students and audiences of all ages. James Heazlewood-Dale  is a Grammy-nominated bassist and a professor at Brandeis University, where he lectures on film music and video game history. Originally from Sydney, Australia, he moved to Boston to pursue studies in jazz double bass at Berklee College of Music and the New England Conservatory, where he received full scholarships. Dr. Heazlewood-Dale has shared the stage with world-renowned artists, including Jacob Collier, Maria Schneider, Grace Kelly, Terence Blanchard, Zakir Hussain, and Mehmet Ali Sanlıkol. He has presented at esteemed national conferences, including those for the American Musicological Society, the Musicological Society of Australia, the Jazz Education Network, and the College Music Society. Notably, he was commissioned by Decca Records to craft the liner notes for the soundtrack release of The Callisto Protocol (2022) and featured as a scholarly guest in Adam Neely's acclaimed video essay "The Nintendo-fication of Jazz." Drummer  Paul July Joseph  is from Port-au-Prince, Haiti, and is currently studying Contemporary Musical Arts at the New England Conservatory of Music. He recently won a major award from the Percussive Arts Society, and has competed in Drumfest, Le Batteur, and Drum-Off Global. He has worked with Silkroad’s Global Musician Workshop, has performed at the Panama Jazz Festival, and recently joined Akili Jamal Haynes and World of Chibuzo for a performance at Carnegie Hall, sponsored by the United Nations. His drum teachers have included Prosper Prevoit, Austin MacMahon, and Obed Calvaire. Paul is currently working on a project, Creole Jazz Fusion, which blends Haitian folk styles such as Yanvalou, Congo, Ibo, Kompa, and Zouk with jazz. He performs regularly with ensembles led by Itay Dayan, Sam Saomek Srithongkum, and Mark Tipton.   www.marktiptonmusic.com   facebook.com/markalantipton @mark.tipton.music

events.title: TCS presents: Sam Miller
events.description:
18+ w/ 2-Item Suggested Minimum. Please Arrive Early to Guarantee Seating.




Sam Miller
 is a nationally touring comedian from Olympia, Washington. He is 6 foot 6, 360 pounds, has two kids, (one of them is on purpose) he's been married for 15 years, and has been clean and sober for 17 years. Sam likes to make jokes about what it's like to be a sober parent. He also likes to make jokes about what jails like in Yakima. His first album and special, Round Trip, was recorded and filmed under the tutelage of Grammy-winning producer Dan Schlissel, whose indie label, Stand Up! Records, Sam had recently signed a three-album deal with. Round Trip was released October 27th 2023 and immediately went to number one on the iTunes Comedy Charts. It even broke into the top 200 overall charts. Sam is a recurring guest and has been heard by an estimated 2.5 million listeners on the nationally syndicated "Bob & Tom Radio Show." He has written for Newsweek. He was the runner-up in the 2021 Seattle International Comedy Competition and won the Comedy on Trial Competition in 2017. He has headlined multiple major comedy clubs including Sidesplitters in Tampa, Helium in Portland, and The Laugh Factory and Zanies in Chicago. He's also performed with the Addicts Comedy Tour and at NA and AA conventions all over the country. For three consecutive years, he won awards in "The Best of Olympia" issue of the Weekly Volcano.
2016 Best Local Hero / 2017 Best Local Celebrity / 2018 Best Comic Relief

events.title: Hatha Yoga w/ Live Music
events.description:
$20-$25 at the door / $15 students & seniors / 12pm start  Experience the magic of a moving meditation with Integral Yoga instructor Vienna-Parashakti. This 90-minute class is appropriate for all students, from beginners to advanced yogis. Dress comfortably, and bring a cozy blanket if you’d like. (cash or venmo accepted at the door) 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Prepare to relax and rejuvenate your body, mind, and spirit in this peaceful yoga class. Explore the guided practice of Hatha Yoga and experience a series of classical Yoga asanas (physical postures), pranayama (breath control), Yoga Nidra (deep relaxation) and meditation.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Parashakti  (Vienna) is an Integral Yoga instructor and a new-ish resident to Cambridge from two and a half years studying and teaching at  Satchidananda Ashram  in Yogaville, Virginia.  She is currently teaching weekly Hatha Yoga classes at the Lilypad and other places around Cambridge. 
 
 
 
 
 
 Musical accompaniment on the Grand Piano provided by Jesse Gallagher, along with selections from his meditation album "The Inner Sound." 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 “ It was such a delight to attend your class.  My nervous system has been a wreck and it was wonderful to be in a place that felt safe for my body.  I haven’t moved my “yogi” body in years and it felt so good to wake up the cobwebs. Thank you for providing such a beautiful space for me in a day that I really needed it. ” 
 
 — Maria 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Yoga Classes at Lilypad continue weekly on Saturdays.

Join the West End Museum and the Museum of African American History for a discussion series on two plays that examines the cycle of Black migration, white flight, urban renewal, displacement, and gentrification in Chicago’s changing neighborhoods.    First, read Lorraine Hansberry’s classic play A Raisin in the Sun, a Black family drama set on the South Side of Chicago. The Younger family lives in poverty, but when a life insurance payment offers them a chance to change their situation, they face the question of how to achieve their deferred dreams. Do they invest in business, education, or a home in a white neighborhood? Discuss how redlining, poverty, and neglect of urban neighborhoods has affected Black communities.    Next read Bruce Norris’s Claybourne Park, a new perspective on Hansberry’s story that follows a white family selling their home in a quiet neighborhood in Chicago. It soon becomes clear that they are selling to the Younger family prompting discussions on block busting, white flight, the American Dream, and what happens when the cycles of urban change come to affect the same house and communities.    This two part book club is open to all.    Reserve a free ticket to join with your own copies of the plays or select paid tickets and pick up copies of each book at the West End Museum. events.description: Register here Nebula's spooky season book club! Join us as we read & discuss  Slewfoot: A Tale of Bewitchery  over craft beers at the Idle Hands taproom (non-alcoholic options available). A paid ticket includes a BRAND NEW copy of the book, or you can register for free and bring your own (if you prefer a non-physical format, you can support us by purchasing through our affiliate links on  Bookshop.org  or  libro.fm )! Meetings will be held on 9/30, 10/14, and 10/28. Copies of the book will be distributed at the first meeting; if you're not able to make that session, contact us to set up an alternate pickup time. Register here Book description: A  USA TODAY  BESTSELLER! Set in Colonial New England,  Slewfoot  is a tale of magic and mystery, of triumph and terror as only dark fantasist Brom can tell it. Connecticut, 1666: An ancient spirit awakens in a dark wood. The wildfolk call him Father, slayer, protector. The colonists call him Slewfoot, demon, devil. To Abitha, a recently widowed outcast, alone and vulnerable in her pious village, he is the only one she can turn to for help. Together, they ignite a battle between pagan and Puritan – one that threatens to destroy the entire village, leaving nothing but ashes and bloodshed in their wake. This terrifying tale of bewitchery features more than two dozen of Brom’s haunting full-color paintings and brilliant endpapers, fully immersing readers in this wild and unforgiving world.

 Musical accompaniment on the Grand Piano provided by Jesse Gallagher, along with selections from his meditation album "The Inner Sound."

I haven’t moved my “yogi” body in years and it felt so good to wake up the cobwebs. Thank you for providing such a beautiful space for me in a day that I really needed it. ” 
 
 — Maria

events.description: TICKETS AVAILABLE HERE Children of the night, assemble! You are summoned by your elders to pass their vampire tests and prove yourself worth to survive Halloween. events.title: Toad Sunday Revival - Tim Gearan Band
events.description: A beloved fixture in the Boston music scene for over 25 years, Tim Gearan has become a bonafide local music hero. His warm, raspy baritone, jaw-dropping guitar skills and wry, poignant songwriting have graced the bars, pubs, and music halls throughout New England and beyond, creating a loyal cult-like following. Gearan, a New York native, spent ten years touring the globe as a sideman for the great Toni Lynn Washington, as well as collaborating with Grammy-winning singer/guitarist Susan Tedeschi. Finding his own artistic voice, Gearan  has crafted an intoxicating blend of Americana, folk and blues with shades of Randy Newman, Tom Waits, JJ Cale,  Leon Russell and Lowell George. He quickly established himself as a force in the Boston’s resurgent roots music scene, and his Boston area residencies have become a “can’t miss” staple of the city’s nightlife. Gearan has released 7 albums to date, as well as 4 single releases; “While the World Goes By” (2019)  “It’s Not the End of the World"  (2019) “Hey, Hey, Hey” (2020) and “Talk About Heaven” (2020).

events.description:
$25 at the door / $20 in advance / $15 students and seniors / 7:30 doors / seated 
 
 
 
 
    Get Tickets
   
 
 
 
 
 
 Lafayette Gilchrist featuring special guest and Cambridge native, Cecil Brooks of the Sun Ra Arkestra. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Lafayette Gilchrist’s music draws on the span of jazz history from stride to free improvisation, along with inspiration from hip-hop, funk, and Washington D.C.’s unique go-go sound. His work thrives on making surprising connections between styles and influences, boldly veering from piledriver funk to piquant stride, vigorous swing to hip-hop swagger, contemplative abstraction to deep-bottom grooves. Gilchrist is the pianist in the Sun Ra Arkestra, has toured extensively with David Murray, and his compositions have graced the soundtracks of David Simon’s acclaimed series The Wire, The Deuce, and Treme. Gilchrist has performed with Cassandra Wilson, Macy Gray, Oliver Lake, Andrew Cyrille, Orrin Evans, Paul Dunmall, Hamid Drake, William Parker and many more. Gilchrist’s second solo recording, 2019 “Dark Matter” which muses on the elusive and mysterious matter that ties the universe together, landed on numerous critics best of lists. Gilchrist returns to The Lilypad, where he played for a standing room only crowd in 2022, for a performance featuring a special guest appearance by Cambridge native and fellow member of the Sun Ra Arkestra, Cecil Brooks on trumpet. www.lafayettegilchrist.com

events.title: UPSTAIRS: Somerville Songwriter Sessions
events.description:
Learn more / Buy Tickets
   
 
 
 
 
 As it has for more than a decade, Somerville Songwriter Sessions presents the finest acoustic singer-songwriters each month in an intimate, welcoming setting. Each concert features three songwriters each doing a solo set, and then trading songs in the round, allowing for stories, impromptu harmonies, jamming, and spontaneous inspiration. Each show, one of our five hosts – Rachel Marie, Terry Kitchen, Sam Bayer, Beth DeSombre, Jack Byrne – are joined by some of the best local and touring singer-songwriters on the scene. November 8: Rachel Marie Rachel Marie (she/they) follows in a tradition of unapologetically forthright femme folksingers, with songs that hearken to "overstuffed lines of Tori Amos, philosophical turn of Indigo Girls, and lilting vocals like Joni Mitchell" (Victoria Farmer, The Christian Humanist Podcast). The social awareness of folk meets the introspection and healing of the singer-songwriter tradition, featuring the emotional catharsis and dynamic vocals of a Broadway show. With a songwriting approach as raw and honest as it's always been, Rachel Marie is making a return to live performance after an unintentional hibernation hiatus, ready to reconnect with a real live audience. December 13: Beth DeSombre Beth DeSombre writes songs that are "smart and  uplifting...focusing on the quiet meaning to be found in ordinary life" (Sing Out! Magazine), exploring issues from the personal to the political. Her music touches both mind and heart, with insights wrapped in melody and harmony that stay with you after the echoes of the last chorus have faded away. Her newest CD Holding the Threads (2024) is her most personal album to date, telling stories about family and crisis and trying to find hope in dark times. Her previous EP The Sea Beside Us (2023), tells stories of ships and the ocean. Her 2017 EP Resistance, which was written in response to the political situation after the 2016 election, is a fundraiser for the ACLU. An award-winning writer in many formats, she has published 8 books. $15 in advance. (+ processing fees) $20 at the door. This Is An All Ages Show Doors are at 3:30pm. Showtime is 4pm. Dinner and drinks available at all tables. NO REFUNDS OR EXCHANGES

events.title: Joe Hunt Group
events.description:
$15 admission / Start 8:30pm / Doors 8pm / Seated Show Modern jazz played by Boston's best jazz musicians. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Joe Hunt  is a jazz drummer, educator, author, and historian. In the early 1960s, Joe Hunt performed and recorded alongside the late NEC Distinguished Artist-in-Residence Emeritus George Russell, with releases on Decca and Riverside. Hunt joined The Stan Getz Quartet in 1964, recording several releases on Verve, then was a member of the Bill Evans Trio from 1966-1967. The remainder of the 1960s found Hunt performing or recording with several other jazz luminaries including Chet Baker, Eric Dolphy, Dizzy Gillespie, Dexter Gordon, Charles Mingus, Bob Brookmeyer, and the late Herb Pomeroy. In the 1970s and 1980s, Hunt was a member of The National Jazz Ensemble, led jazz groups with John Scofield, Mike Stern, and Santi Debriano, and toured with quartets of Red Rodney and Hal McKusick. The 1990s, and beyond, have included membership in The Smithsonian Jazz Masters Orchestra, with former NEC president Gunther Schuller, performances with Kenny Burrell, Joe Lavano, Joanne Brackeen, and Tal Farlow, as well as recordings with the Bert Seager Quintet, and also, Trio. Hunt is the author of the 1994 book 52nd Street Beat, which is a historical look at jazz drummer greats from 1945 to 1965. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 The Joe Hunt quartet features a modern jazz ensemble music played by top local pros: Mark Pinto - alto saxophone, formerly years with the Buddy Rich band John Lockwood – bass, formerly with Joe Henderson, Lee Konitz, current Fringe member Yuka Hamano Hunt – piano, voice, arranger Joe Hunt – drums, formerly with George Russell, Stan Getz, Jim Hall, Dexter Gordon, and Bill Evans We pay tribute to a special composer or performer at most performances. Recent shows have included: Burt Bacharach, Ahmad Jamal, Bill Evans, and Gigi Gryce. Future shows will include the music of Paul and Carla Bley, and arranger, Johnny Mandel. - Continuing of the 3rd Sunday of Every Month

events.description: Dennis Brennan was born on the wrong side of the tracks in Marlboro, Massachusetts. At age 9 he entered show business as Rumplestiltsken in a grammar school play. In 7th grade he performed “Louie Louie” with a local garage band at the Berlin, Ma. Town Hall and quickly evolved into “the lead singer” That band evolved into “The Paranoids”, his musical outlet throughout his high school years. They opened shows for both The Remains and The Barbarians, garage band legends who are each featured on “Nuggets, original artyfacts from the first psychedelic era” Rhino R2 75486. Following high school. Brennan’s education continued as lead singer in such well regarded outfits as “The Dirty Rye Band”, The West Side Band”, “The Martells”, and “Push Push”. These bands performed in every bar and dive on the east coast. An education indeed. In 1992 he formed the Dennis Brennan Band and started his solo career, quickly releasing two critically acclaimed recordings on Upstart Records, a division of Rounder. In 2000 he released “Rule #1” on ESCA Records which resulted in glowing reviews from The New Yorker, The Chicago Sun Times, The Boston Phoenix as well as other publications nationwide. These recordings showcase Brennans ability “to not just tip toes into genres, he strips naked and plunges right in.” Bill Holmes, AMPLIFIER.

events.title: Toad Sunday Revival - Tim Gearan Band
events.description: A beloved fixture in the Boston music scene for over 25 years, Tim Gearan has become a bonafide local music hero. His warm, raspy baritone, jaw-dropping guitar skills and wry, poignant songwriting have graced the bars, pubs, and music halls throughout New England and beyond, creating a loyal cult-like following. Gearan, a New York native, spent ten years touring the globe as a sideman for the great Toni Lynn Washington, as well as collaborating with Grammy-winning singer/guitarist Susan Tedeschi. Finding his own artistic voice, Gearan  has crafted an intoxicating blend of Americana, folk and blues with shades of Randy Newman, Tom Waits, JJ Cale,  Leon Russell and Lowell George. He quickly established himself as a force in the Boston’s resurgent roots music scene, and his Boston area residencies have become a “can’t miss” staple of the city’s nightlife. Gearan has released 7 albums to date, as well as 4 single releases; “While the World Goes By” (2019)  “It’s Not the End of the World"  (2019) “Hey, Hey, Hey” (2020) and “Talk About Heaven” (2020).

events.description:

Jay Jurden
 is the star of the new Hulu comedy special Yes Ma’am, a breakout hour that solidifies him as one of the sharpest and most original comedic voices working today. Based in New York and originally from Mississippi, Jay has become a national standout thanks to his precise writing, magnetic presence, and a point of view that is both deeply personal and universally funny. The special is now available on all streaming platforms. Jay is a four-time guest on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon and has also appeared on The Late Show with Stephen Colbert, The Late Late Show with James Corden, Comedy Central Featuring, and HBO’s High Maintenance. He was a Staff Writer for Apple TV+’s Emmy-nominated The Problem with Jon Stewart, bringing his distinctive comedic insight to one of television’s most influential political-comedy series. In 2022, Jay was named one of Variety’s 10 Comics to Watch, and his debut comedy album Jay Jurden Y’all premiered at #1 on iTunes. His writing has appeared in The New Yorker, Vulture, Teen Vogue, McSweeney’s, and Marvel’s Voices: X-Men #1, showcasing a range that extends well beyond stand-up. Jay was also featured on Vulture’s Comedians You Should and Will Know list and selected for the prestigious Just For Laughs: New Faces.

events.title: UPSTAIRS: Somerville Songwriter Sessions
events.description:
Learn more / Buy Tickets
   
 
 
 
 
 As it has for more than a decade, Somerville Songwriter Sessions presents the finest acoustic singer-songwriters each month in an intimate, welcoming setting. Each concert features three songwriters each doing a solo set, and then trading songs in the round, allowing for stories, impromptu harmonies, jamming, and spontaneous inspiration. Each show, one of our five hosts – Rachel Marie, Terry Kitchen, Sam Bayer, Beth DeSombre, Jack Byrne – are joined by some of the best local and touring singer-songwriters on the scene. December 13: Beth DeSombre Beth DeSombre writes songs that are "smart and  uplifting...focusing on the quiet meaning to be found in ordinary life" (Sing Out! Magazine), exploring issues from the personal to the political. Her music touches both mind and heart, with insights wrapped in melody and harmony that stay with you after the echoes of the last chorus have faded away. Her newest CD Holding the Threads (2024) is her most personal album to date, telling stories about family and crisis and trying to find hope in dark times. Her previous EP The Sea Beside Us (2023), tells stories of ships and the ocean. Her 2017 EP Resistance, which was written in response to the political situation after the 2016 election, is a fundraiser for the ACLU. An award-winning writer in many formats, she has published 8 books. $15 in advance. (+ processing fees) $20 at the door. This Is An All Ages Show Doors are at 3:30pm. Showtime is 4pm. Dinner and drinks available at all tables. NO REFUNDS OR EXCHANGES
