events.title: Toad Sunday Revival - The Dennis Brennan Band
events.description: Dennis Brennan was born on the wrong side of the tracks in Marlboro, Massachusetts. At age 9 he entered show business as Rumplestiltsken in a grammar school play. In 7th grade he performed “Louie Louie” with a local garage band at the Berlin, Ma. Town Hall and quickly evolved into “the lead singer” That band evolved into “The Paranoids”, his musical outlet throughout his high school years. They opened shows for both The Remains and The Barbarians, garage band legends who are each featured on “Nuggets, original artyfacts from the first psychedelic era” Rhino R2 75486. Following high school. Brennan’s education continued as lead singer in such well regarded outfits as “The Dirty Rye Band”, The West Side Band”, “The Martells”, and “Push Push”. These bands performed in every bar and dive on the east coast. An education indeed. In 1992 he formed the Dennis Brennan Band and started his solo career, quickly releasing two critically acclaimed recordings on Upstart Records, a division of Rounder. In 2000 he released “Rule #1” on ESCA Records which resulted in glowing reviews from The New Yorker, The Chicago Sun Times, The Boston Phoenix as well as other publications nationwide. These recordings showcase Brennans ability “to not just tip toes into genres, he strips naked and plunges right in.” Bill Holmes, AMPLIFIER.

events.description:
$15 admission / Start 8:30pm / Doors 8pm / Seated Show Modern jazz played by Boston's best jazz musicians. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Joe Hunt  is a jazz drummer, educator, author, and historian. In the early 1960s, Joe Hunt performed and recorded alongside the late NEC Distinguished Artist-in-Residence Emeritus George Russell, with releases on Decca and Riverside. Hunt joined The Stan Getz Quartet in 1964, recording several releases on Verve, then was a member of the Bill Evans Trio from 1966-1967. The remainder of the 1960s found Hunt performing or recording with several other jazz luminaries including Chet Baker, Eric Dolphy, Dizzy Gillespie, Dexter Gordon, Charles Mingus, Bob Brookmeyer, and the late Herb Pomeroy. In the 1970s and 1980s, Hunt was a member of The National Jazz Ensemble, led jazz groups with John Scofield, Mike Stern, and Santi Debriano, and toured with quartets of Red Rodney and Hal McKusick. The 1990s, and beyond, have included membership in The Smithsonian Jazz Masters Orchestra, with former NEC president Gunther Schuller, performances with Kenny Burrell, Joe Lavano, Joanne Brackeen, and Tal Farlow, as well as recordings with the Bert Seager Quintet, and also, Trio. Hunt is the author of the 1994 book 52nd Street Beat, which is a historical look at jazz drummer greats from 1945 to 1965. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 The Joe Hunt quartet features a modern jazz ensemble music played by top local pros: Mark Pinto - alto saxophone, formerly years with the Buddy Rich band John Lockwood – bass, formerly with Joe Henderson, Lee Konitz, current Fringe member Yuka Hamano Hunt – piano, voice, arranger Joe Hunt – drums, formerly with George Russell, Stan Getz, Jim Hall, Dexter Gordon, and Bill Evans We pay tribute to a special composer or performer at most performances. Recent shows have included: Burt Bacharach, Ahmad Jamal, Bill Evans, and Gigi Gryce. Future shows will include the music of Paul and Carla Bley, and arranger, Johnny Mandel. - Continuing of the 3rd Sunday of Every Month

events.title: Allan Chase Quartet
events.description:
$15 admission / 6pm doors / 6:20 start / seated Original jazz compositions by the members of the band. Allan Chase - alto & soprano saxophones Nate Radley - guitar Bruno Råberg - bass Gen Yoshimura - drums 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Allan Chase  is a saxophonist and composer who has performed jazz and improvised music since 1974 with his own groups and as a member of the Lewis Nash-Allan Chase Duo (1979-80), Your Neighborhood Saxophone Quartet (1981-2018), Prima Materia with Rashied Ali (1992-2000), the Steve Lantner Quartet with Joe Morris and Luther Gray, the Bruno Råberg Quartet and Tentet, and the Ayn Inserto Jazz Orchestra. He appears as a soloist on over sixty jazz and improvised music recordings, several rock and classical recordings, and several movie scores. Chase began teaching at Berklee in 1981 and served as chair of Ear Training there (2008-21). He has also taught at Tufts and NEC, where he served as chair of Jazz Studies, dean of faculty, and chair of Contemporary Improvisation, and continues to teach jazz history courses. 
 
 
 
 more info:  allanchase.com

events.title: Orkest
events.description:
Founded in 2022 by Sapphire Skye Toth and Michael Gehman while they earned their Master of Science degrees in Arts Administration at Boston University, Orkest is meant to be the place where New Music meets The Community and The Community meets New Music.

Orkest, a visionary musical venture rooted in the bustling city of Boston, is on a mission to redefine the local music scene. Recognizing the abundance of untapped musical talent, Orkest seeks to bridge the gap between emerging composers and the community, breaking away from classical traditions and creating an inviting space for diverse genres. Departing from conventional models, Orkest utilizes venues to bring people to music, not just vice versa, fostering a casual environment in cafe bars and libraries. With a commitment to equitable treatment of artists, creating opportunities for artists at socioeconomic disadvantages, professional recordings of performances, and a unique pay-what-you-wish model, Orkest is not just a music experience; it's a transformative force shaping how communities engage with and appreciate new music and the artists who create it.

 (2014, 2015),

(2015),

 (2015, 2017, 2019), Showtime's

(2017), TruTv's

events.title: JAZZ NIGHT: Dave Fox Trio
events.description:
The Dave Fox Trio is a Modern Jazz Trio featuring original jazz
compositions and arrangements inspired by artists such as John Coltrane, Joe Henderson, Chick Corea, Steve Swallow, Charles Mingus, Thelonious Monk and Wayne Shorter. The group features internationally acclaimed bassist John Lockwood and innovative Boston area musicians and composers such as guitarist Phil Sargent and saxophonists Nicholas Brust and Bill Jones.

Dave Fox is an accomplished, versatile drummer and is currently a full-time member of The Gravel Project, Dan Rockett and The Guilty Party and
“AS3” along with Andrew Stern and Brad Barrett.

As a sideman for over two decades, he has performed with a diverse group of artists including Jerry Bergonzi, John Lockwood, Josh Smith, Dave Tronzo, Charles Neville, Stan Strickland, The Stompers and Tom Hambridge and The Rattlesnakes to name a few.

events.title: Ricky Stein
events.description: Austin-born singer/songwriter Ricky Stein writes songs that seek to find spiritual common ground between the mesas of West Texas and the streetscapes of the world's great music capitals. Original compositions such as "Night Shines On," "American Dreaming," and "The Great Empty" capture the energy of urban life in the modern era; latest single "Heart of the Night" seeks hope and meaning through human connection. All songs are delivered in an earnest baritone accompanied by acoustic guitar, harmonica, and a good-humored stage presence.

past_events.title: UPSTAIRS: Somerville Songwriter Sessions
past_events.description:
Learn more / Buy Tickets
   
 
 
 
 
 As it has for more than a decade, Somerville Songwriter Sessions presents the finest acoustic singer-songwriters each month in an intimate, welcoming setting. Each concert features three songwriters each doing a solo set, and then trading songs in the round, allowing for stories, impromptu harmonies, jamming, and spontaneous inspiration. Each show, one of our five hosts – Rachel Marie, Terry Kitchen, Sam Bayer, Beth DeSombre, Jack Byrne – are joined by some of the best local and touring singer-songwriters on the scene. September 13: Sam Bayer Cambridge-based smartass troubadour Sam Bayer is your literate, exuberant guide to an imaginary world where housewives win the Nobel Prize in physics, poker-playing children gamble over their bedtimes, and metaphorical elephants pirouette in the den, four and a half minutes at a time. His latest studio CD, Bad Apple, brings 11 gems from his universe to yours. October 11: Terry Kitchen Called "one of New England's best songwriters" by The Boston Globe, Terry Kitchen has been performing on folk stages across the country since the 1990s, releasing a dozen albums filled with literate musical storytelling, supple guitar playing and distinctive, intimate vocals. His 2025 album We All Dream (with its title song reaching the top ten of the national Folk-DJ chart) offers a hard-won glimmer of hope just when we need it most. His songs have won the Mid-Atlantic and USA Song Contests and been runner-up in the John Lennon Song Contest, and have appeared in numerous films. In the 1980s he was the leader of the groundbreaking Boston band Loose Ties, whose experiences he recounts in his novel Next Big Thing, called "a great debut novel" by The San Francisco Book Review. "Terry Kitchen begins where Tom Waits and Elvis Costello merge and leave off."-Vance Gilbert November 8: Rachel Marie Rachel Marie (she/they) follows in a tradition of unapologetically forthright femme folksingers, with songs that hearken to "overstuffed lines of Tori Amos, philosophical turn of Indigo Girls, and lilting vocals like Joni Mitchell" (Victoria Farmer, The Christian Humanist Podcast). The social awareness of folk meets the introspection and healing of the singer-songwriter tradition, featuring the emotional catharsis and dynamic vocals of a Broadway show. With a songwriting approach as raw and honest as it's always been, Rachel Marie is making a return to live performance after an unintentional hibernation hiatus, ready to reconnect with a real live audience. December 13: Beth DeSombre Beth DeSombre writes songs that are "smart and  uplifting...focusing on the quiet meaning to be found in ordinary life" (Sing Out! Magazine), exploring issues from the personal to the political. Her music touches both mind and heart, with insights wrapped in melody and harmony that stay with you after the echoes of the last chorus have faded away. Her newest CD Holding the Threads (2024) is her most personal album to date, telling stories about family and crisis and trying to find hope in dark times. Her previous EP The Sea Beside Us (2023), tells stories of ships and the ocean. Her 2017 EP Resistance, which was written in response to the political situation after the 2016 election, is a fundraiser for the ACLU. An award-winning writer in many formats, she has published 8 books. $15 in advance. (+ processing fees) $20 at the door. This Is An All Ages Show Doors are at 3:30pm. Showtime is 4pm. Dinner and drinks available at all tables. NO REFUNDS OR EXCHANGES

$10 admission / 4pm doors / 4:30 show / standing IMAGINE  is a door to longing, wonder, stillness, anger, ecstasy, love… all the feelings that exist within all of us. This performance is a place to soften, to drift, to remember something you may have forgotten. Take this invitation to surrender to the beauty of uncertainty and rawness, and to discover what can emerge when we allow ourselves to simply imagine. What if this is all a dream? And what if this dream is the truest place you've ever been? Leo Vee 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Leo is a powerful sound-sorceress. Resentful from the maltreatment she experienced growing up, he left his hometown to live in a cabin, deep in the forest. By day he sings through his flute to the wildlife. By night she creates sound-sorcery and spells; planning vengeance upon all who have hurt her. She fights to preserve her intrinsic playfulness & steadfast spirit, but every so often, darkness inevitably consumes him and he unleashes it in a cold fury; upon those who have done terrible things. He was awarded full-tuition scholarships to study at Berklee College of Music for both undergraduate and graduate degrees, earning his graduate degree from the extremely exclusive Berklee Global Jazz Institute under the direction of master pianist, educator and humanitarian Danilo Perez. An equally important part of his education was down the street from Berklee at Boston’s historic Wally’s Jazz Cafe. He began going to jam sessions there in high school and eventually became the house bass player every Friday and Saturday night. Ridley has played and recorded with renowned musicians of many different styles all over the world.  An incredibly versatile multi-instrumentalist, Max performs regularly in bands playing Jazz, Rock, Folk, Soul, Punk, Klezmer, Polka and every other style you can think of.  He also serves as the music director for tap dance company Subject:Matter ( https://www.subjectmattertap.com/ ) and teaches music as a guest lecturer at different colleges around New England (such as Longy School of Music, University of New Hampshire and Berklee College of Music).  A fine, high-powered tenor saxophonist with a tone influenced by John Coltrane, a mastery of chord changes, and a strong musical imagination,  Jerry Bergonzi  has long had an underground following in the Boston area. He started on clarinet when he was eight, switching to alto at 12, and finally to tenor two years later. Bergonzi was inspired early on by Sonny Rollins, Coltrane, and Hank Mobley. He attended Lowell University and then after graduation played electric bass in local bands behind singers and strippers, saving up enough money to move to New York in 1972. After struggling in the Big Apple for seven years and gaining some recognition as a member of Two Generations of Brubeck and of the Dave Brubeck Quartet (with whom he appeared on several Concord albums during 1979-1981), Bergonzi moved back to Boston in 1981, where he developed a strong career both as a tenorman and as an educator. He has since led several groups (including two called Con Brio and Gonz) and recorded for the Plug, Not Fat, Red, and Blue Note labels. —  By Scott Yanow, AllMusic

Pat Donaher's Demodacus
past_events.description: $20 admission / 7:30 doors / seated & standing / all ages Saxophonist and composer  Pat Donaher  returns to the Lilypad with a reimagining of one of his oldest projects,  Demodacus . It will be an evening of original music, some new and some from Donaher’s debut as a leader in the late 90s,  all inspired by Homer’s  Odyssey. Musicians:: Pat Donaher- woodwinds Zoe Murphy- trumpet Caio Aiofune- guitar Ian Ashby- bass Lee Fish- drums Donaher has been enchanted by the Odyssey since a young age, inspired by his classicist father.  For his first performances at New York’s legendary Knitting Factory in 1999, he assembled a book of music largely inspired by the  Odyssey  featuring some of New York’s hottest young players.  For this performance he has expanded the book to reflect his awe of Emily Wilson’s translation, and recruited some of Boston’s finest players to interpret it- Zoe Murphy on trumpet, Caio Afiune on guitar, Ian Ashby on bass, and Lee Fish on drums.   Downbeat magazine called Donaher’s recent album  Occasionally  “an occasion unto itself, a dual showcase for Donaher’s alto playing and compositional chops…”  Featuring an all-star lineup of Allison Miller, Jason Palmer, Carmen Staaf and Tony Scherr, the album visits a series of seminal events in Donaher’s life.  Donaher has also released three other recordings, and performed with a wide range of musicians, from Benny Carter to Steve Vai.  There is a $20 cover charge, and beer and wine will be served.  The Lilypad is located on  1353 Cambridge Street  in Inman Square.  For more information please contact Pat Donaher at  617-721-0741  or  pat@patdonaher.com Social media: @patdonaher     Facebook event:  https://www.facebook.com/events/1811372793201550

past_events.title: Jesse Gallagher  + Steve Fell
past_events.description:
$10 admission / 7pm / seated show Jesse Gallagher  began living above the Lilypad in 2006, just a few blocks from where his grandfather grew up on Inman st.  At the time Jesse was in the middle of what would be about a decade of regular touring, performing & recording with his psychedelic rock band Apollo Sunshine.  The band was featured in the New York Times, Rolling Stone, Spin & shared the stage with legendary acts  Wu-Tang Clan ,  Toots & The Maytals ,  The Flaming Lips  &  Dr. Dog . Jesse has been involved with the Lilypad for 20 years and the full time talent booking agent since 2013. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Breaking Bad used Jesse’s song “We are Born When We Die” (2008) to dramatic effect. “Today is the Day” (2005) was in international Nike commercials while his “Singing to the Earth to Thank Her For You” was used in a large GAP campaign. Gallagher has collaborated, recorded & performed extensively w/  Sam Cohen ,  Willy Mason ,  Lilys ,  Nick Nicely ,  Doug Tuttle  &  Edan . Gallagher is a certified Yoga & Meditation teacher and hosts classes at the Lilypad & online. Since 2018, he has released 40 pieces of instrumental music which have been used in millions of YouTube videos ranging from NBC NY to Tesla and most recently a string of viral videos by Emma Chamberlain. Gallagher has a very active YouTube channel, making lots of psychedelic music videos and building a community of mindful listeners. @jessegallagher.tv Steve Fell  is a guitarist, composer, and educator whose performing and recording career over the last twenty five years has reached across the boundaries of jazz, experimental, funk, free form improvisation, rock, electronic, reggae/calypso, hip-hop, psych, and many others.   
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 He co-leads the groups  Clear Audience, Quantum Banditos, Dome Room,  and  Astronomico,  leads a trio under his own name, and collaborates with numerous bands and artists. @stevefellmusic
